body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). If \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{r_1(\Sigma)\}\) on \(\mathcal K_G\), then with probability tending to one uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}\) has exactly one element; that element is consistent and asymptotically normal with the scalar variance given by the corresponding diagonal entry of the covariance matrix in \(\mathrm{thm:regular\mbox{-}finite\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}inference}\).
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)=\{r_1(\Sigma)\}\) throughout \(\mathcal K_G\).  On the events \(\mathcal H_m\) supplied by the regular finite-set inference theorem, the estimated retained set is bijectively matched to the population retained set.  Hence it has exactly one element, say \(\widehat r_m\), and
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\!\left(
   \widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{\widehat r_m\}
 \right)\longrightarrow1.                                     \tag{44}
\]
Define \(\widehat r_m=0\) when the estimated set is not a singleton.  By (44), this extension changes the statistic only on an event whose probability tends to zero uniformly.

For singleton sets, Hausdorff distance is absolute error.  The Hausdorff-rate conclusion of the regular finite-set inference theorem therefore gives, on \(\mathcal H_m\),
\[
 |\widehat r_m-r_1(\Sigma)|
 =d_H\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m},
              \mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\right)
 =O_{\mathbb P}(m^{-1/2})                                      \tag{45}
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).  Together with (44), this proves uniform consistency of the extended statistic.

Taking the first coordinate in the joint branch limit of the regular finite-set inference theorem yields
\[
 \sqrt m\{\widehat r_m-r_1(\Sigma)\}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,W_{11}(\Sigma)),                          \tag{46}
\]
where
\[
 W(\Sigma)
 =Dr(\Sigma)D\pi_G(\Sigma)V_\Sigma
  D\pi_G(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}Dr(\Sigma)^{\mathsf T}.            \tag{47}
\]
The uniformly negligible modification outside \(\mathcal H_m\) does not alter (46).  The variance \(W_{11}(\Sigma)\) is the corresponding diagonal entry required by the proposition; if it is zero, (46) is the degenerate centered normal law and no additional nondegeneracy premise is needed.
body.justification: The singleton case connects finite-set inference to the familiar direct-effect estimator and Wald limit.
body.gap: Regular half-trek asymptotic normality covers rationally identified coefficients, whereas this corollary also covers a singleton real projection of a higher complex-degree coordinate polynomial.
body.consumer: When only one real supported branch survives, applied users obtain an ordinary point estimate, standard error, and confidence interval.
